subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from Mpho Mansour's 1892 novel The Counter at Belgrave's. The narrator and two colleagues are clerks behind the counter of a London haberdashery.

Behind a shop counter, I have always observed that it is the settled conviction of every clerk that he alone attends to the customers. Pemberton's view was, that it was he who had waited on every gentleman who crossed the threshold, and that Collins and I had merely lingered about pretending to be useful. Collins, for his part, dismissed the notion that Pemberton had done anything beyond rearranging the ribbon drawer, and held an unshakable opinion that it was he—Collins himself—who had borne the whole weight of the afternoon's trade.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It establishes Pemberton's feelings about the narrator's idea of how shop work usually proceeds.
choices.B: It suggests that Pemberton is making an effort to help resolve a disagreement among the clerks.
choices.C: It indicates that Pemberton finds his experiences behind the counter to be puzzling.
choices.D: It offers Pemberton's belief as a specific example of a trend the narrator has observed while working as a clerk.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The passage opens with the narrator's general observation that behind a shop counter, 'it is the settled conviction of every clerk that he alone attends to the customers.' The underlined sentence then presents Pemberton's specific belief—that he alone had waited on every gentleman while Collins and the narrator merely pretended to be useful—as one concrete instance of this general pattern. The following sentence offers Collins's parallel belief as another example. The underlined sentence thus functions to illustrate the trend the narrator has observed.
